name: Italian Game
description: A practical 1.e4 course that starts with the classic Italian setup, then teaches simple responses to common Black defenses.

branches.title: Main Line: Italian Setup
branches.description: Learn the default beginner Italian setup before studying deviations.

moves.title: Claim the center
moves.explanation: Controls d5 and f5, opens the bishop and queen, and starts the game by fighting for central space instead of making a slow side move. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. After the Italian setup, finish development, castle, and only then prepare c3-d4 or pressure on f7.

moves.title: Black mirrors the center
moves.explanation: Black also fights for central space. This creates an open position where quick development matters. e5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. After the Italian setup, finish development, castle, and only then prepare c3-d4 or pressure on f7.

moves.title: Develop with a threat
moves.explanation: Develops a knight, attacks e5, and prepares castling. This avoids the beginner mistake of bringing the queen out too early.

moves.title: Black defends e5
moves.explanation: Black develops while defending the e5 pawn. White should continue improving pieces, not chase pawns. Nc6 develops a knight to c6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Point at f7
moves.explanation: Develops the bishop to an active diagonal, prepares castling, and creates natural pressure on f7 without forcing an attack too soon.

ideas: Learn the main Italian setup first.
Against c5, c6, e6, or d5, respond with center control and development.
Your goal is confidence in real beginner games, not memorizing engine lines.
After the Italian setup, finish development, castle, and only then prepare c3-d4 or pressure on f7.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Panicking when Black does not play e5.
Moving the queen early instead of building pieces.
Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
